cap_enforced_flag.meaning: _processLimitAskOrder() enforces a hard cap maxNumLimitsPerSide on active ask orders per side
cap_enforced_flag.checkpoint: before posting a valid limit order

expired_orders_resident.meaning: expired limit orders remain resident in the ask book and are not filtered or removed before the capacity check
expired_orders_resident.checkpoint: before posting a valid limit order

valid_order_rejected.meaning: a valid competitive limit order is denied because the book is perceived as full even though resident orders are inactive or expired

selective_denial.meaning: malicious actors selectively deny participation for specific price ranges or actors because the expiration range is not checked at order posting

assumptions: Posting limit orders is permissionless, so malicious actors can occupy book space with expired orders.
The per-side cap is reached by resident expired orders before a valid order is posted.
Expired orders can be created and left resident in the ask book.

unresolved.description: No explicit numeric value for maxNumLimitsPerSide or the number of expired orders needed to fill the cap; the cap relation is represented qualitatively.
Report does not state who may post expired orders or whether posting is permissionless.

limitations: The cap and expired-order occupancy are represented as grounded Boolean observables because the report gives no numeric cap value or order counts.
The attack ordering (occupy then post) is inferred from the griefing narrative rather than explicitly sequenced.
Only the censorship impact is formalized; other impacts are handled in separate passes.
